paragraphs.sourceText: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write a letter to express your thanks to your parents or any family members upon making memorable achievement. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在这部分，你有30分钟的时间写一封信，表达你对父母或任何家庭成员在取得令人难忘的成就时的感谢。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Part ⅢReading Comprehension (40 minutes)
paragraphs.translationZh: 第三部分阅读理解（40分钟）

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the center. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Signs barring cell-phone use are a familiar sight to anyone who has ever sat in a hospital waiting room. But the 26 popularity of electronic medical records has forced hospital-based doctors to become 27 on computers throughout the day, and desktops—which keep doctors from bedsides—are 28 giving way to wireless devices.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于任何曾经坐在医院候诊室的人来说，禁止使用手机的标志都是熟悉的景象。但电子病历的日益普及迫使医院的医生全天依赖电脑，而台式机（使医生无法在床边）正在迅速让位于无线设备。

paragraphs.sourceText: As clerical loads increased, “something had to 29 , and that was always face time with patients,” says Dr. hakti Patel, a former chief resident in the University of Chicago’s internal-medicine program. In fall 2010, she helped 30 a pilot project in Chicago to see if the iPad could improve working conditions and patient care. The experiment was so 31 that all internal-medicine program adopted the same 32 in 2011. Medical schools at Yale and Stanford now have paperless, iPad-based curriculums. “You’ll want an iPad just so you can wear this” is the slogan for one of the new lab coats 33 with large pockets to accommodate tablet computers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着文书工作量的增加，“必须做出一些牺牲，那就是与患者面对面的时间，”芝加哥大学内科项目前首席住院医师哈克蒂·帕特尔博士说。 2010 年秋天，她帮助在芝加哥启动了一个试点项目，看看 iPad 是否可以改善工作条件和患者护理。该实验非常成功，以至于所有内科项目在 2011 年都采用了相同的政策。耶鲁大学和斯坦福大学的医学院现在都拥有基于 iPad 的无纸化课程。 “你需要一台 iPad，这样你就可以穿上它”，这是一款新型实验室外套的口号，该外套设计有大口袋，可容纳平板电脑。

paragraphs.sourceText: A study of the University of Chicago iPad project found that patients got tests and 34 faster if they were cared for by iPad-equipped residents. Many patients also 35 a better understanding of the illnesses that landed them in the hospital in the first place.
paragraphs.translationZh: 芝加哥大学 iPad 项目的一项研究发现，如果患者得到配备 iPad 的居民的照顾，他们可以更快地接受检查和治疗。许多患者也对最初导致他们入院的疾病有了更好的了解。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Ancient Greek Wisdom Inspires Guidelines to Good Life
paragraphs.translationZh: 古希腊智慧启发美好生活的准则

paragraphs.sourceText: A. Is it possible to enjoy a peaceful life in a world that is increasingly challenged by threats and uncertainties from wars, terrorism, economic crises and a widespread outbreak of infectious diseases? The answer is yes, according to a new book The 10 Golden Rules: Ancient Wisdom from the Greek Philosophers on Living a Good Life. The book is co-authored by Long Island University’s philosophy professor Michael Soupios and economics professor Panos Mourdoukoutas.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：在一个日益受到战争、恐怖主义、经济危机和传染病大范围爆发的威胁和不确定性挑战的世界里，是否有可能享受和平的生活？根据新书《十大黄金法则：希腊哲学家关于美好生活的古代智慧》的说法，答案是肯定的。该书由长岛大学哲学教授迈克尔·苏皮奥斯（Michael Soupios）和经济学教授帕诺斯·穆杜库塔斯（Panos Mourdoukoutas）共同撰写。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. The wisdom of the ancient Greek philosophers is timeless, says Soupios. The philosophy professor says it is as relevant today as when it was first written many centuries ago. “There is no expiration ( 失效) date on wisdom,” he says, “There is no shelf life on intelligence. I think that things have become very gloomy these day, lots of misunderstanding, misleading cues, a lot of what the ancients would have called sophistry ( 诡辩 ). The nice thing about ancient philosophy as offered by the Greeks is that they tended to see life clear and whole, in a way that we tend not to see life today.” Examine your life
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 苏皮奥斯说，古希腊哲学家的智慧是永恒的。这位哲学教授说，它在今天和许多世纪前首次写成时一样具有现实意义。 “智慧没有失效期，”他说，“智力没有保质期。我认为现在的情况变得非常悲观，有很多误解、误导性暗示，还有很多古人所说的诡辩。希腊人提供的古代哲学的好处在于，他们倾向于以一种我们今天看不到的方式来看待生活。”检查你的生活

paragraphs.sourceText: C. Soupios, along with his co-author Panos Mourdoukoutas, developed their 10 golden rules by turning to the men behind that philosophy—Aristotle, Socrates, Epictetus and Pythagoras, among others. The first rule—examine your life—is the common thread that runs through the entire book. Soupios says that it is based on Plato’s observation that the unexamined life is not worth living. “The Greeks are always concerned about boxing themselves in, in terms of convictions ( 信念 ),” he says. “So take a step back, switch off the automatic pilot and actually stop and reflect about things like our priorities, our values, and our relationships.” Stop worrying about what you can not control
paragraphs.translationZh: C. Soupios 和他的合著者 Panos Mourdoukoutas 向该哲学背后的人物——亚里士多德、苏格拉底、爱比克泰德和毕达哥拉斯等人求助，制定了他们的 10 条黄金法则。第一条规则——审视你的生活——是贯穿整本书的共同主线。苏皮奥斯说，这是基于柏拉图的观察，未经审视的生活不值得过。 “希腊人总是担心自己在信念方面陷入困境，”他说。 “所以退一步，关掉自动驾驶仪，真正停下来反思一下我们的优先事项、我们的价值观和我们的关系等事情。”不再担心你无法控制的事情

paragraphs.sourceText: D. As we begin to examine our life, Soupios says, we come to Rule No.2: Worry only about things that you can control. “The individual who promoted this idea was a Stoic philosopher. His name is Epictetus,” he says. “And what the Stoics say in general is simply this: There is a larger plan in life. You are not really going to be able to understand all of the dimensions of this plan. You are not going to be able to control the dimensions of this plan.”
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 苏皮奥斯说，当我们开始审视自己的生活时，我们就得出了第二条规则：只担心你可以控制的事情。 “提出这个想法的人是一位斯多葛派哲学家。他的名字叫爱比克泰德，”他说。 “斯多葛学派的一般说法很简单：生活中有一个更大的计划。你实际上无法理解这个计划的所有维度。你将无法控制这个计划的维度。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E. So, Soupios explains, it is not worth it to waste our physical, intellectual and spiritual energy worrying about things that are beyond our control. “I can not control whether or not I wind up getting the disease swine flu, for example.” He says. “I mean, there are some cautious steps I can take, but ultimately I can not guarantee myself that. So what Epictetus would say is sitting at home worrying about that would be wrong and wasteful and irrational. You should live your life attempting to identify and control those things which you can genuinely control.” Seek true pleasure
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 因此，苏皮奥斯解释说，浪费我们的体力、智力和精神能量来担心我们无法控制的事情是不值得的。 “例如，我无法控制自己是否会感染猪流感。”他说。 “我的意思是，我可以采取一些谨慎的步骤，但最终我不能向自己保证这一点。所以爱比克泰德会说，坐在家里担心这将是错误的、浪费的和非理性的。你应该在生活中尝试识别和控制那些你真正可以控制的事情。”寻求真正的快乐

paragraphs.sourceText: F. To have a meaningful, happy life we need friends. But according to Aristotle—a student of Plato and teacher of Alexander the Great—most relationships don’t qualify as true friendships. “Just because I have a business relationship with an individual and I can profit from that relationship, it does not necessarily mean that this person is my friend,” Soupios says. “Real friendship is when two individuals share the same soul. It is a beautiful and uncharacteristically poetic image that Aristotle offers.”
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 为了拥有有意义、幸福的生活，我们需要朋友。但根据柏拉图的学生、亚历山大大帝的老师亚里士多德的说法，大多数关系并不算是真正的友谊。 “仅仅因为我与某人有业务关系并且我可以从这种关系中获利，并不一定意味着这个人是我的朋友，”苏皮奥斯说。 “真正的友谊是两个人拥有相同的灵魂。这是亚里士多德所描绘的美丽而异常的诗意形象。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G. In our pursuit of the good life, he says, it is important to seek out true pleasures—advice which was originally offered by Epicurus. But unlike the modern definition of Epicureanism as a life of indulgence ( 放纵 ) and luxury, for the ancient Greeks, it meant finding a state of calm, peace and mental ease.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 他说，在我们追求美好生活的过程中，寻找真正的快乐很重要——这一建议最初是由伊壁鸠鲁提出的。但与伊壁鸠鲁主义现代定义为放纵和奢侈的生活不同，对于古希腊人来说，它意味着寻找一种平静、平和和精神轻松的状态。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. “This was the highest and most desirable form of pleasure and happiness for the ancient Epicureans,” Soupios says. “This is something that is very much well worth considering here in the modern era. I do not think that we spend nearly enough time trying to concentrate on achieving a sort of calmness, a sort of contentment in mental and spiritual way, which was identified by these people as the highest form of happiness and pleasure.” Do good to others
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 苏皮奥斯说：“对于古代伊壁鸠鲁主义者来说，这是最高、最令人向往的快乐和幸福形式。” “这是在现代非常值得考虑的事情。我认为我们没有花费足够的时间来试图集中精力实现一种平静，一种精神和精神上的满足，而这些人认为这是幸福和快乐的最高形式。”为他人做好事

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Other golden rules counsel us to master ourselves, to avoid excess and not to be a prosperous ( 发迹的 ) fool. There are also rules dealing with interpersonal relationships: Be a responsible human being and do not do evil things to others.
paragraphs.translationZh: I. 其他黄金法则建议我们控制自己，避免过度，不要成为一个成功的傻瓜。处理人际关系也有规则：做一个负责任的人，不做恶事。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. “This is Hesiod, of course, a younger contemporary poet, we believe, with Homer,” Soupios says. “Hesiod offers an idea—which you very often find in some of the world’s great religions, in the Judeo-Christian tradition and in Islam and others—that in some sense, when you hurt another human being, you hurt yourself. That damaging other people in your community and in your life, trashing relationships, results in a kind of self-inflicted ( 自己招致的 ) spiritual wound.”
paragraphs.translationZh: J. “当然，这是赫西奥德，我们相信，他是一位年轻的当代诗人，与荷马一样，”苏皮奥斯说。 “赫西奥德提出了一个观点——你在世界上一些伟大的宗教、犹太基督教传统、伊斯兰教和其他宗教中经常会发现这一点——从某种意义上说，当你伤害另一个人时，你就伤害了自己。伤害你社区和生活中的其他人，破坏人际关系，会导致一种自我造成的精神创伤。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K. Instead, Soupios says, ancient wisdom urges us to do good. Golden Rule No.10 for a good life is that kindness toward others tends to be rewarded.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 苏皮奥斯说，相反，古老的智慧敦促我们行善。美好生活的黄金法则第十条是，善待他人往往会得到回报。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. “This is Aesop, the fabulist ( 寓言家 ), the man of these charming little tales, often told in terms of animals and animal relationships,” he says. “I think what Aesop was suggesting is that when you offer a good turn to another human being, one can hope that that good deed will come back and sort of pay a profit to you, the doer of the good deed. Even if there is no concrete benefit paid in response to your good deed, at the very least, the doer of the good deed has the opportunity to enjoy a kind of spiritually enlightened moment.”
paragraphs.translationZh: L. “这是寓言家伊索，他创作了这些迷人的小故事，这些故事经常以动物和动物关系的形式讲述，”他说。 “我认为伊索的意思是，当你向另一个人提供善意时，人们可以希望这份善行能够回报你，并为你这个善行者带来某种利润。即使你的善行没有得到任何具体的回报，至少，善行的行者有机会享受一种精神上的启蒙时刻。”

paragraphs.sourceText: M. Soupios says following the 10 Golden Rules based on ancient wisdom can guide us to the path of the good life where we stop living as onlookers and become engaged and happier human beings. And that, he notes, is a life worth living. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: M. Soupios 表示，遵循基于古代智慧的 10 条黄金法则可以引导我们走上美好生活的道路，让我们不再以旁观者的身份生活，而是成为积极参与、更快乐的人。他指出，这才是值得过的生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. According to an ancient Greek philosopher, it is impossible for us to understand every aspect of our life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 根据一位古希腊哲学家的说法，我们不可能了解生活的方方面面。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Ancient Philosophers saw life in a different light from people of today.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 古代哲学家以与现代人不同的眼光看待生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Not all your business partners are your soul mates.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 并非所有的商业伙伴都是你的灵魂伴侣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. We can live a peaceful life despite the various challenges of the modern world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 尽管现代世界面临各种挑战，我们仍能过上和平的生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. The doer of a good deed can feel spiritually rewarded even when they gain no concrete benefits.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 做好事的人即使没有获得任何具体的好处，也会感到精神上的回报。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. How to achieve mental calmness and contentment is well worth our consideration today.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41、如何达到心灵的平静和知足，很值得我们今天思考。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Michael Soupios suggests that we should stop and think carefully about our priorities in life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. Michael Soupios 建议我们应该停下来仔细思考我们生活中的优先事项。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Ancient philosophers strongly advise that we do good.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43.古代哲学家强烈建议我们行善。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. The wise teachings of ancient Greek thinkers are timeless, and are applicable to contemporary life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 古希腊思想家的智慧教义是永恒的，并且适用于当代生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Do harm to others and you do harm to yourself.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 伤害别人就是伤害自己。

paragraphs.sourceText: Direction: There are two passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the center.
paragraphs.translationZh: 方向：本节有两段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Attitudes toward new technologies often fall along generational lines. That is, generally, younger people tend to outnumber older people on the front end of a technological shift.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对新技术的态度通常会随着代际的变化而变化。也就是说，一般来说，在技术变革的前沿，年轻人的数量往往超过老年人。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is not always the case, though. When you look at attitudes toward driverless cars, there doesn’t seem to be a clear generational divide. The public overall is split on whether they’d like to use a driverless car. In a study last year, of all people surveyed, 48 percent said they wanted to ride in one, while 50 percent did not.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但情况并非总是如此。当你观察人们对无人驾驶汽车的态度时，你会发现似乎并没有明显的代际鸿沟。公众对于是否愿意使用无人驾驶汽车总体上存在分歧。去年的一项研究显示，在所有接受调查的人中，48% 的人表示他们想乘坐一辆汽车，而 50% 的人则不愿意。

paragraphs.sourceText: The fact that attitudes toward self-driving cars appear to be so steady across generations suggests how transformative the shift to driverless cars could be. Not everyone wants a driverless car now—and no one can get one yet—but among those who are open to them, every age group is similarly engaged.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，几代人对自动驾驶汽车的态度似乎都很稳定，这表明向无人驾驶汽车的转变可能会带来多大的变革。现在并不是每个人都想要一辆无人驾驶汽车——而且还没人能得到一辆——但在那些对无人驾驶汽车持开放态度的人中，每个年龄段的人都同样参与其中。

paragraphs.sourceText: Actually, this isn’t surprising. Whereas older generations are sometimes reluctant to adopt new technologies, driverless cars promise real value to these age groups in particular. Older adults, especially those with limited mobility or difficulty driving on their own, are one of the classic use cases for driverless cars. This is especially interesting when you consider that younger people are generally more interested in travel-related technologies than older ones.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，这并不奇怪。尽管老一辈人有时不愿意采用新技术，但无人驾驶汽车尤其为这些年龄段的人带来了真正的价值。老年人，尤其是行动不便或难以自行驾驶的老年人，是无人驾驶汽车的经典用例之一。考虑到年轻人通常比年长的人对旅行相关技术更感兴趣，这一点尤其有趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: When it comes to driverless cars, differences in attitude are more pronounced based on factors not related to age. College graduates, for example, are particularly interested in driverless cars compared with those who have less education: 59 percent of college graduates said they would like to use a driverless car compared with 38 percent of those with a high-school diploma or less.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当谈到无人驾驶汽车时，基于与年龄无关的因素，态度差异更加明显。例如，与受教育程度较低的人相比，大学毕业生对无人驾驶汽车特别感兴趣：59% 的大学毕业生表示他们希望使用无人驾驶汽车，而高中及以下学历的人中这一比例为 38%。

paragraphs.sourceText: Where a person lives matters, too. More people who lives in cities and suburbs said they wanted to try driverless cars than those who lived in rural areas.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一个人住在哪里也很重要。与居住在农村地区的人相比，更多居住在城市和郊区的人表示他们想尝试无人驾驶汽车。

paragraphs.sourceText: While there’s reason to believe that interest in self-driving cars is going up across the board, a person’s age will have little to do with how self-driving cars can become mainstream. Once driverless cares are actually available for sale, the early adopters will be the people who can afford to buy them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管有理由相信人们对自动驾驶汽车的兴趣正在全面上升，但一个人的年龄与自动驾驶汽车如何成为主流几乎没有关系。一旦无人驾驶护理真正开始销售，早期采用者将是那些有能力购买它们的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. What happens when a new technology emerges?
paragraphs.translationZh: 46.当新技术出现时会发生什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. What does the author say about the driverless car?
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 作者对无人驾驶汽车有何评价？

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. Why does the driverless car appeal to some old people?
paragraphs.translationZh: 48.为什么无人驾驶汽车对一些老年人有吸引力？

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. What is likely to affect one’s attitude toward the driverless car?
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 什么可能会影响一个人对无人驾驶汽车的态度？

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. Who are likely to be the first to buy the driverless car?
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 谁可能最先购买无人驾驶汽车？

paragraphs.sourceText: Question 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 51 至 55 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: In agrarian ( 农业的), pre-industrial Europe, “you’d want to wake up early, start working with the sunrise, have a break to have the largest meal, and then you’d go back to work,” says Ken Albala, a professor of history at the University of the Pacific, “Later, at 5 or 6, you’d have a smaller supper.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 在农业化、工业化之前的欧洲，“你会想早起，在日出时开始工作，休息一下，吃一顿丰盛的饭菜，然后再回去工作，”太平洋大学历史学教授肯·阿尔巴拉说，“后来，在五点或六点，你会吃一顿少一点的晚餐。”

paragraphs.sourceText: This comfortable cycle, in which the rhythms of the day helped shape the rhythms of the meals, gave rise to the custom of the large midday meal, eaten with the extended family. “Meals are the foundation of the family,” says Carole Counihan, a professor at Millersville University in Pensylvania, “so there was a very important interconnection between eating together” and strengthening family ties.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在这种舒适的循环中，一天的节奏有助于塑造膳食的节奏，从而产生了与大家庭一起吃午餐的习俗。 “膳食是家庭的基础，”宾夕法尼亚州米勒斯维尔大学教授卡罗尔·库尼汉说，“因此一起吃饭”和加强家庭关系之间存在着非常重要的相互联系。

paragraphs.sourceText: Since industrialization, maintaining such a slow cultural metabolism has been much harder, with the long midday meal shrinking to whatever could be stuffed into a lunch bucket or bought at a food stand. Certainly, there were benefits. Modern techniques for producing and shipping food led to greater variety and quantity, including a tremendous increase in the amount of animal protein and dairy products available, making us more vigorous than our ancestors.
paragraphs.translationZh: 自工业化以来，维持如此缓慢的文化新陈代谢变得更加困难，漫长的午餐减少到可以塞进午餐桶或在食品摊上购买的任何东西。当然，这是有好处的。现代食品生产和运输技术带来了更多的品种和数量，包括动物蛋白和乳制品的数量大幅增加，使我们比我们的祖先更有活力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Yet plenty has been lost too, even in cultures that still live to eat. Take Italy. It’s no secret that the Mediterranean diet is healthy, but it was also a joy to prepare and eat. Italians, says Counihan, traditionally began the day with a small meal. The big meal came at around 1 p.m. In between the midday meal and a late, smaller dinner came a small snack. Today, when time zones have less and less meaning, there is little tolerance for offices’ closing for lunch, and worsening traffic in cities means workers can’t make it home and back fast enough anyway. So the formerly small supper after sundown becomes the big meal of the day, the only one at which the family has a chance to get together. “The evening meal carries the full burden that used to be spread over two meals,” says Counihan.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，即使在仍然以饮食为生的文化中，也有很多东西已经消失了。以意大利为例。众所周知，地中海饮食是健康的，但准备和食用也是一种乐趣。库尼汉说，意大利人传统上以一顿小餐开始新的一天。大餐是在下午 1 点左右来的。在中午的正餐和较晚的、较小的晚餐之间，有一份小零食。如今，时区的意义越来越小，人们几乎无法容忍办公室因午餐而关闭，而城市交通状况的恶化意味着工人们无论如何也无法足够快地回家和返回。因此，日落后原本的小晚餐变成了一天中的大餐，是全家人唯一有机会聚在一起的一顿饭。 “过去，晚餐的全部负担是由两顿饭承担的，”库尼汉说。

paragraphs.translationZh: 51.我们从有关前工业化欧洲的人们的文章中学到了什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. What does Professor Carole Counihan say about pre-industrial European families eating meals together?
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 卡罗尔·库尼汉教授对工业化前的欧洲家庭一起吃饭有何看法？

paragraphs.translationZh: 53. “文化新陈代谢”（第 1 行第 3 段）指的是什么？

paragraphs.translationZh: 55.作者对过去的意大利人有何评价？
